otawara_lower_p161_right.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八（大田原）
otawara_lower_p161_right.page_topic: Fascicle-8 domain-officials roster (governor and councillors) — the data belongs to Ōtawara domain (大田原藩), NOT Wakayama despite the batch label
otawara_lower_p161_right.page_summary_en: This is a Fascicle-8 (officials) page of the Hansei Ichiran, listing the appointed administrative officers of a single domain. The running header in the outer margin reads 藩制一覧表第八（大田原）and the governor (知事) is the hereditary daimyo 大田原一學 (Ōtawara Ichigaku), so the data on this page belongs to OTAWARA DOMAIN (大田原藩, a small ~11,400-koku fudai domain in Shimotsuke), NOT to Wakayama/Kii as the batch-prep label ('Wakayama / 和歌山藩') asserts — this is a domain-attribution mismatch that should be corrected upstream. The roster records one 知事 (大田原一學), one 大参事 (阿久津正右衛門), one 権大参事 (金枝仲), five 少参事 (伊王野守人・阿久津丈右衛門・藤田六郎・大谷長太郎・阿久津長右衛門), and three 権少参事 (権田等・江連幸三郎・松本豊之助); rank headings carry their appointee counts (少参事五, 権少参事三). A small-print editorial variant note (一…二要人ニ作ル) sits beside the fifth 少参事 name. The MASTER batch-prep entry carried only an 'AUDIT' placeholder with no extracted field values, so every value here was read directly from the scan; the printed page number in the outer margin is 二百九十八 (298).

hirosaki_lower_p097_right.page_topic: Fascicle-7 boundary page: tail of the previous domain's population/religious/warship fields, then the head of Hirosaki-han's (弘前藩) fiscal block (kokudaka, land tax, totals, households).
hirosaki_lower_p097_right.page_summary_en: DOMAIN MISMATCH: the batch record keys this page as Hiroshima (廣島藩), but the scan contains NO Hiroshima data. The running header in the outer margin reads 藩制一覧表第七（弘前）(Fascicle 7, Hirosaki), and the sole maru-marker on the page is ○弘前藩 元高十萬石 (Hirosaki-han, original assessment 100,000 koku). Applying the right-of-marker rule, the five right-hand columns (僧侶修驗 clergy, 穢多非人 outcastes, 神社 shrines, 知事家族 governor's family, 船艦 warships) are the closing fields of the PREVIOUS domain, whose own marker and governor name fall on the preceding page and are not printed here; everything at and to the left of the ○弘前藩 marker (草高 assessed kokudaka 274,482 koku incl. reclaimed land, 正租 land tax 130,854.5 koku as a five-year average, 雜税 misc. tax in rice and money, 合〆 grand totals in rice and money, 戸數 50,162 households) is Hirosaki-han. Sub-koku places follow 石=斗(0.1)升(0.01); the (マ、) glyph beside the eta-hinin total is an editorial sic mark, and the printed page number in the bottom margin is 百七十 (170).

shonai_upper_p065_right.page_topic: Okayama domain population and household breakdown by status group, grand totals, shrines/temples, and one warship (Fascicle 2 demographics).
shonai_upper_p065_right.page_summary_en: This page carries the tail of the Okayama domain (岡山藩) entry in Fascicle 2 of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran, ending at the ○大泉藩 boundary marker in the lower left where the next domain (Ōizumi) begins — so every data column to the right of that marker is Okayama's. It records the commoner population of 328,341 (male 172,475 / female 155,874) and, by status group, the Shinto-priest households and population (642 / 2,772), temple population (709), mountain-ascetic households and population (105 / 323), and outcaste (eta) households and population (993 / 9,128, the latter noted as including preachers and burial workers). Grand totals are 85,431 households and 358,827 persons; the domain reports 701 shrines and 464 temples, plus one warship (the entrusted vessel Kawachi). The outer-margin running header names Ōizumi as the page's provenance, and the printed page number in the bottom margin is 104.

shonai_lower_p149_right.page_header_en: Table of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 8 (Ōizumi section)
shonai_lower_p149_right.page_topic: Okayama domain officials (councillors and administrative ranks) and standing military force, at the boundary with the Ōizumi domain entry.
shonai_lower_p149_right.page_summary_en: This is a fascicle-8 page recording domain officials and military strength. Although the running header names the Ōizumi (大泉) section, the ○大泉藩 boundary marker sits mid-page, so everything to its RIGHT belongs to the previous domain, Okayama (岡山藩): eight named councillors (議員), the administrative rank headings 少参事 (junior counsellor) and 権少参事 (acting junior counsellor), and Okayama's standing army — seventeen rifle battalions (十七大隊 銃隊), four artillery emplacements (四坐 砲隊), totaling 7,862 personnel (此人員七千八百六拾貳人). The 知事 (governor) heading to the LEFT of the ○大泉藩 marker introduces the next domain, Ōizumi. Faint 岡山藩 characters in the upper-middle are verso bleed-through, not ink on this page.

kokura_lower_p143_right.page_topic: Fascicle-8 officials-and-military boundary page: Tottori's overflow (權少参事 officials + army) at right, and the start of Kōharu's block at left.
kokura_lower_p143_right.page_summary_en: This is a fascicle-8 (officials and military) page whose running header and boundary marker both name Kōharu (○香春藩), making it a two-domain boundary page. Content to the RIGHT of the ○香春藩 marker is the overflow tail of the PREVIOUS domain, Tottori (鳥取藩): its 權少参事 rank with six appointees (杉浦清五郎, 四宮要, 津田優也, 角田拾藏, 荒尾十郎, 加藤尚) and its army — 10 battalions of 3,734 men (十大隊 人員三千七百三十四人) plus an artillery corps of 240 men (砲隊 貳百四十人). Content to the LEFT of the marker begins Kōharu's own block: governor (知事), one senior councillor (大参事 一員), four deputy senior councillors (權大参事 四員), and its own force of 46 companies totalling some 2,700 men (四十六小隊 此人員二千七百人余). MASTER keyed this page to Tottori and captured only the two Tottori military fields, which are verified here; the officials columns and the Kōharu block are added.

tsu_upper_p150_right.page_topic: Tsu domain civil data (fascicle 4): revenue totals, kokudaka accounting, population, households, and status-class counts with male/female splits
tsu_upper_p150_right.page_summary_en: This is the right half of the Hansei Ichiran fascicle-4 civil spread for Tsu domain (津藩, Ise province), book page 274. No fresh ○-marker opens on this half-page, so every column continues Tsu's own record. The right cluster gives the fiscal accounting: two gold (金) tax lines (415 ryō and 437 ryō), the rice total 合米 (126,451.102 koku), the gold-to-rice conversion 此米 (87.512 koku, reckoned at 2 koku of rice per 10 ryō), and their grand total 合 (126,538.614 koku = 126,451.102 + 87.512). The left cluster records households (戸數 52,513), total population (人口 247,682), and the status classes shizoku, gōshizoku, sotsuzoku, imperial-tomb guards (御陵守), shrine officials (社務人), and Buddhist monks (僧), each with a male/female breakdown. Two master values were misread and are corrected here: the first 金 is 415 ryō (四百拾五兩), not 437; and 戸數 is 52,513 (五萬貳千五百十三軒), not 52,543.

tsuyama_upper_p150_left.page_topic: Civil register (kokudaka, land tax, vessels, temples/shrines, outcaste and clerical populations) — Tsuyama domain opening on this leaf, with the tail of the previous domain Tsu on the right.
tsuyama_upper_p150_left.page_summary_en: This civil-register leaf of Han'sei Ichiran fascicle 4 (printed page 275) carries the tail of the previous domain, Tsu (津藩), on the right of the ○津山藩 marker, then opens the entry for Tsuyama (津山藩) to its left. Tsu's trailing fields here are demographic/status and infrastructure counts: soldiers (兵卒) 1,647; one steamship plus one sailing/transport vessel; 579 villages; 1,247 temples; 1,122 shrines; hinin 1,564 and eta 9,098 (each with a male/female split); and 52 nuns, closed by a submission note dated Kōgo (1870) 11th month, 13th day. Tsuyama's own opening fields give a base koku (高) of 100,000, a reclaimed/re-surveyed add-on (込高新田改出高) of 4,576.913 koku, a total kusadaka (草高) of 104,576.913 koku, and a main land tax (正租) of 41,967.4508 koku of rice averaged over five years (from the horse-year to the dragon-year). Because the marker opens the entry, the book labels this leaf 津山; the right-of-marker fields are tagged to Tsu.

morioka_lower_p113_right.page_topic: 人口 (population / demographics), plus opening kokudaka and land-tax columns of the next domain
morioka_lower_p113_right.page_summary_en: This CIVIL half-page from fascicle 7 (人口 / demographic register) carries two domains split by the ○森藩 domain marker at center. The columns to the RIGHT of the marker complete the demographic block of Morioka (盛岡藩): total population 117,527 (male 61,314 / female 56,213), the eta-household count (31 戸), the domain-administered-land population of 189 persons (male 100 / female 89), the 支配地人口戸數 sub-header, and the 24,515-household count, all under a 審ナラス ('not surveyed in detail') notation. To the LEFT of the ○森藩 marker begin the fiscal columns of the neighbouring Mori domain (森藩): 草高 12,500 石, an 外 (additional) 1,774.64306 石, 合高 (total) 14,274.64306 石, and 正租米 (land-tax rice) 5,165.59044 石 averaged over the five years 甲子(1864)–戊辰(1868). The running head reads 藩制一覽表第七 (森) and the bottom-margin page number is 202.

mori_lower_p113_left.page_topic: Mori Domain (森藩) civil statistics — continuation: retainer-class households/populations, domain kokudaka taxes (soybean, misc-tax rice, gold, ei), total households, and population with male/female splits
mori_lower_p113_left.page_summary_en: This is the left (continuation) half of the two-page civil entry for Mori Domain (森藩), a small ~12,500-koku domain in Bungo Province held by the Kurushima (久留島) family; the domain's ○marker (○森藩) and header open on the facing right half (lower_p113_right.jpg), so this half carries no marker and is read right-to-left as a continuation. NOTE: the MASTER grounding labels this page "Morioka" — that is a misidentification (盛岡 vs 森); the footer keyword 「森」, the marker ○森藩, and the 12,500-koku 草高 on the right half confirm the domain is Mori. The recorded figures are the domain's own core population (14,244; male 6,839 / female 7,405), its shizoku and sotsu households and populations, total households (2,645), and its tax/product yields — soybean (1,205.278 koku), miscellaneous-tax rice (262.216 koku), gold (245 ryō 1 bu 3 shu), and ei (17.122 mon) — followed by a note that the original recorded (in vermillion) the gold-and-rice equivalents (此金5,140 ryō 2 bu / 此米642 koku). Two corrections against MASTER: the sotsu-population male count reads 男三百八十四人 (384, not 382), and the miscellaneous-tax-rice figure reads 貳百六拾貳石 (262, matching the already-correct parsed value; MASTER's raw string 貳百四拾六 was a misread).

tsushima_upper_p017_right.page_topic: Tsushima (Izuhara) domain sundry expenditures: Wakan-and-two-checkpoints expense block, itemized rice/cash breakdown, and the opening of the drifted-persons relief expense item
tsushima_upper_p017_right.page_summary_en: This is a civil expense-detail continuation page for Izuhara (Tsushima) domain, from Fascicle 1 of the Hansei Ichiran (page 8). The right side records the ○和館兩關所入費 expense block — costs of the Wakan (the domain's Japanese trading factory at Pusan in Korea) together with its two barrier checkpoints (関所) — giving a combined total 金ニ〆56,618 ryō 1 bu 2 shu / 銀6匁9分5厘3毛, resolved into a 米 (rice) component of 819.17258 koku and a 錢 (copper cash) component of 815 kan 43 mon, with a small annotation that these are the annual public-trade office-revenue figures. A 此小譯 ('breakdown of the above') then itemizes the component sub-amounts (米321石, 錢473貫; 米498石, 錢341貫) with two 但-notes explaining that the money covers salary-rice, brush/ink/paper/oil/wax, and year-round sundry expenses for officials stationed at the two checkpoints and at the Wakan beachside. At the far left the next expense item, ○漂民入費并飯米 (expenses for shipwrecked/drifted persons plus rice rations), is opened; its figures continue on the facing page (upper_p017_left).

tsushima_upper_p017_left.page_topic: Tsushima domain (嚴原藩): itemized breakdown and explanatory notes for special expenditures on castaway relief and Korea repatriation / Nagasaki ship costs
tsushima_upper_p017_left.page_summary_en: This half-page is a continuation of the Tsushima (Izuhara, 嚴原藩) entry in Fascicle 1 of the Hansei Ichiran, confirmed by the bottom-margin marker 藩制一覧表第一（嚴原）. Rather than the standard kokudaka/demographic table, it records special fiscal figures in rice (米, in koku) and copper cash (錢, in 貫/文) headed by 此小譯 ("the itemized breakdown of this"). The figures cover expenses unique to Tsushima's diplomatic role: rice-and-miso provisions and shipboard costs for hosting drifting castaways (漂民), collecting them from Nagasaki, and repatriating them by ship to Korea (朝鮮國ニ送還). The prose notes (但…、右同斷、同斷) qualify each pair of figures and cross-reference earlier lines; the page number is 九.

numata_lower_p148_right.page_topic: Domain officials (chiji and sanji ranks) and military strength
numata_lower_p148_right.page_summary_en: This is the officials-and-military page (Fascicle 8) for Numata han (沼田藩, Kozuke Province), NOT Okayama as the MASTER record was labeled — the printed header explicitly reads 藩制一覧表第八 （沼田）. The two-register layout lists the administrative ranks across the top band (知事 governor, 大参事 2, 権大参事 2, 少参事 5) with appointee names in the lower band; the 知事 (governor) slot carries no printed name, and the nine printed names fill the 大参事/権大参事/少参事 rolls exactly (2+2+5=9). At the left the military entry records a garrison of 二百五十一人 (251 troops) organized as 三小隊半 (3.5 platoons), with a note that each platoon including officers totals 66 men. The bottom-margin page number is 二百七十二 (272); this is a clean single-domain leaf with no ○marker and no overflow from an adjacent domain.

yoshimi_lower_p176_right.page_topic: Domain officials and military (職員兵隊) — Yoshii officials/troops overflowing right of the Yoshimi marker, plus the opening of the Yoshimi entry
yoshimi_lower_p176_right.page_summary_en: This is the right half of Hansei Ichiran Vol. 2, fascicle 8 (officials and military), physical page 328. The domain marker physically printed on this half is ○吉見藩 (Yoshimi), so Yoshimi is the primary domain; its entry opens here with the 知事 (governor, name not printed on this half) and 大参事 一員 (one senior councillor), continuing onto the facing left half. Per the officials-page overflow convention, everything to the RIGHT of the ○吉見藩 marker belongs to the PREVIOUS domain, 吉井藩 (Yoshii): its lower-rank tallies (少参事 3, 権大参事 2, 権少参事 3, the latter two marked 午二月届 = reported in the 2nd month of the horse year), its 兵員 百七十八員 (178 military personnel), the roster of nine named officials (久住一昌, 石上季親, 高橋恭秀, 松下高勝, 横山信六, 八尾収三, 松下相馬, 青木柔郎, 坂部文左衞門), and two small interlinear collation notes (一ニ松下高橋ナシ = "in one copy Matsushita and Takahashi are absent"; 久住ヲ少参事トス = "Kuzumi is treated as a shōsanji"). The MASTER label "Yoshii" for this half is therefore imprecise: the marker on this half is 吉見 (Yoshimi), while the Yoshii material is overflow.

yoshii_lower_p176_left.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八 （吉井、高鍋）
yoshii_lower_p176_left.page_topic: Domain officials and military establishment (fascicle 8): Yoshimi overflow, Yoshii (no data), and Takanabe
yoshii_lower_p176_left.page_summary_en: This is an officials-and-military page from Hansei Ichiran fascicle 8, read right to left, spanning three domains. The rightmost four rank columns (権大参事 2, 少参事 1, 権少参事 1, 銃兵 30) sit to the RIGHT of the ○吉井藩 marker and are the overflow tail of the PREVIOUS domain, Yoshimi (吉見藩), whose entry opened on the facing right-hand page. The ○吉井藩 (Yoshii) header itself carries the small annotation 審ナラス ("not investigated/not detailed"), so Yoshii records no official or troop counts. The remainder of the page is Takanabe (高鍋藩): 大参事 2 (appointees 城勇雄 and 黒水鷲郎), 権大参事 1 (appointee 坂田蒡), plus its military — rifle infantry of 5 platoons (64 men each), and 1 artillery unit of 54 gunners with 6 cannon.

nobeoka_lower_p199_right.page_summary_en: This is the officials-and-military page for Nobeoka domain (延岡藩, Hyuga province), governed by Naito Masanori (内藤政學), from fascicle 9 of the Hansei Ichiran; the printed book-page number is 374. Reading right-to-left, the ○延岡藩 marker opens Nobeoka; its appointee ranks are Governor (1: Naito Masanori), Senior Councillor / o-sanji (2: Hotaka Shin'ichiro and Oshima Mizen), Acting Senior Councillor / gon-o-sanji (1: Hara Kotaro, annotated as recorded elsewhere as o-sanji), and Junior Councillor / sho-sanji (5), plus a separate list of eight gon-o-sanji reported by the caretaker-official (留守官届). Nobeoka's military (兵隊) totals 878: upper-and-lower samurai troops 345, upper-and-lower foot-soldier troops 503, and 6 cannon with 30 gunners. The three fields to the RIGHT of the ○延岡藩 marker — 官員不詳 (officials not detailed), 兵卒 159, and 郷兵 175 — are right-of-marker overflow belonging to the PREVIOUS domain in fascicle 9, not to Nobeoka.

nomura_lower_p199_left.page_summary_en: This left half of physical page 375 (fascicle 9, 藩制一覧表第九) of the Hansei Ichiran carries the officials-and-military entry for Nomura Domain (○野村藩), opened by its circle marker. Nomura's ranked establishment is a governor (知事, one, no appointee name printed), one senior councillor (大参事, 石川武, with a second appointee 有竹裕 annotated 議員兼 "concurrently a councillor"), two junior senior councillors (権大参事, 小山小隼太 and 松浦晋), and three junior councillors (少参事, 大高周, 立川東太郎, 傍島登); its forces are two infantry platoons of 87 men (兵隊二小隊八十七人) and an artillery unit of six guns and 40 men (砲隊砲六門四十人). To the right of Nomura's marker the columns belong to the PREVIOUS domain, Nobeoka (延岡藩, whose main entry is on the facing right half-page 374): the tail of Nobeoka's junior councillors (少参事: 長谷川秀七, 鈴木才藏, 今村新兵衛, 藁谷丼藏, 大島新四郎) and its junior sub-councillors (権少参事: 堀秀實, 相木森之助, 加藤伊織), which overflow leftward past the marker. The military counts (兵隊 87, 砲隊 40, 大砲 6 門) match the sparse MASTER grounding values.

yamaga_lower_p207_right.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第九（山上、山家）
yamaga_lower_p207_right.page_topic: Domain officials (chiji through gon-shōsanji, with appointee names and a kōginin) and military strength for Yamagami-han and Yamaga-han
yamaga_lower_p207_right.page_summary_en: This is an officials-and-military page from fascicle 9 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表第九), whose running head names the two domains it covers: 山上 (Yamagami) and 山家 (Yamaga). Contrary to the MASTER label ("Yachi"), no Yachi entry appears here. The ○marker opens ○山家藩 (Yamaga-han); everything to its right (rank headings, appointee names, and the 兵隊 military block) belongs to the PREVIOUS domain, 山上藩 (Yamagami-han), per the right-to-left officials-page convention. Yamagami lists 知事1/大参事1/権大参事2/少参事/権少参事 with named appointees (Takagi Seibei, Nakamura Isamu, Mori Naoki, Tanabe Junzō), a kōginin (Tamura Sabun) and two further names (Inagaki Isojirō, Yagi Takeshi), plus military of 士族36 + 卒族61 (=97); Yamaga lists 知事1/大参事2/権大参事2/少参事4 with appointees Sahara Shin'ichi, Fuse Shōgo, Shimizu Daikei, Dōke Yōzō, and further names Tamaru Kōhei and Ōshima Yoshinobu. The bottom-margin printed page number is 390.

yatabe_lower_p207_left.page_topic: Domain officials (governor and councillors) with appointee names, plus military notation, for Yatabe, Yachi, and Matsue
yatabe_lower_p207_left.page_summary_en: This is an officials-and-military page from the ninth fascicle (第九) of the Hansei Ichiran-hyō, read right-to-left. The primary domain is Yatabe (○谷田部藩), whose full official roster is printed: one governor (知事 一人), one senior councillor (大参事 一人), three acting senior councillors (権大参事 三人), and four junior councillors (少参事 四人), together with eight named appointees (Kumagai Ichinoshin the governor, the public-assembly delegate Kumagai Teizō, Ōhinata Kiyohiro, Mitsuoka Kinzaemon, Ido Tōshirō, Nakamura Yūzō, Sekiguchi Tanzō, and Magome Tadashichirō); Yatabe's troop strength is recorded as not detailed (兵隊未詳). The page also carries the opening entries for two neighbouring domains: Yachi (○谷地藩), for which officials and troop numbers are both undetailed (職員兵數不詳), and Matsue (○松江藩), which shows a governor (知事 一人) with its remaining data continuing onto the next page. A caption at left names the fascicle and its three domains (谷田部、谷地、松江), and the bottom margin bears the printed book page number 391.
